category_info.fruit_size_at_harvest: 2-4 cm berries depending on variety and growing conditions
category_info.ripening_signs: fully red with no white shoulders near the calyx, glossy surface, slight fragrance, detaches easily when pulled gently
category_info.time_to_first_fruit: 4-6 weeks after flowering; bare-root plants fruit within 60-90 days of planting
category_info.pollination: self-fertile but needs insects or gentle air movement to set well-shaped fruit
category_info.pruning_season: remove runners throughout the season; renovate beds after final harvest
category_info.watering_need: 2.5 cm of water per week, keep the crown dry and fruit off wet soil
category_info.sunlight_need: full sun, at least 6 hours daily

observations.symptom: Small reddish-purple blotches on upper leaf surface
observations.evidence: Discrete purple spots 2-3 mm wide with lighter centers, clearly visible in the photo

observations.symptom: Healthy white flowers and developing green fruit
observations.evidence: Multiple open blossoms and small green berries are present and undamaged

possible_causes.name: Strawberry leaf scorch (Diplocarpon earlianum)
possible_causes.reason: Irregular purple blotches on leaf tops are typical of leaf scorch, common in warm wet weather

possible_causes.name: Minor physiological stress or aging foliage
possible_causes.reason: Older leaves naturally develop purple tinges when nutrient levels fluctuate

recommended_actions.action: Remove and dispose of the most affected leaves; mulch with straw to keep fruit off the soil
recommended_actions.reason: Reduces spore splash from soil to foliage and improves airflow around the crown

recommended_actions.action: Water at soil level in the morning and avoid wetting leaves and fruit
recommended_actions.reason: Leaf scorch and grey mold both need wet leaf surfaces to establish

recommended_actions.action: Re-check in one week before considering any treatment
recommended_actions.reason: Low severity; many strawberry leaf blotches stay cosmetic and do not reduce yield

seasonal_context: Late spring flowering coincides with peak fungal pressure in humid regions; dry airflow protects the developing berries.
what_to_monitor: Spots enlarging or merging into large purple areas
Any grey fuzzy mold on flowers or ripening berries
limitations: Spot diseases of strawberry look alike from a distance; close-up photos improve accuracy
Fruit ripeness and taste quality cannot be judged from leaves alone
follow_up_questions: How closely are the plants spaced, and is there straw mulch under them?
Have the berries shown any soft brown patches after rain?
